PullRequest.Title: agentHost: support Git branch naming settings
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Related to #321685.

Agent Host worktree branches currently add an `agents/` namespace even when a Git branch prefix is configured. Add `chat.agentHost.branchName.useGitSettings` (default: `false`) to opt in to Git's prefix and, for local sessions, its existing random naming settings.

- Use the configured Git prefix without adding `agents/`; retain prompt-derived naming when random naming is unavailable or disabled.
- Reuse Git's branch-name sanitization and check collisions against the final candidate. Use the repository returned by opening, rather than falling back to an open parent repository.
- Carry prepared naming through session configuration and later branch creation, including workspace conversion and folder-session PR creation. Keep existing branches and default-off behavior unchanged.

## Validation

- Broader Agent Host/provider selection: **914 passing, 12 pending**. After the optional Git-error fallback fix, the full local-provider suite was rerun: **551 passing, 11 pending**.
- Effective-prefix regressions verified failing before the fix; schema filtering with Git naming enabled verified through creation and first send (**7 focused provider tests passed**).
- Full Git extension suite: **102 passing, 2 pending**.
- `npm run build-fast`, `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run gulp compile-extension:git`, and `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p extensions/git/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **passed**.
- Changed-file ESLint, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and whitespace checks: **passed**.
- Live verification in a Codespace desktop: a local Copilot session created a worktree branch using the configured prefix and random naming, without adding `agents/`.

### Manual testing

1. Enable `chat.agentHost.branchName.useGitSettings` and `git.branchRandomName.enable`, and set `git.branchPrefix` to `validation/`.
2. Start a new local Agent Host session in a Git repository and select **New Worktree**.
3. Ask the agent to run `git branch --show-current`. The branch should use `validation/` and a random name, without an added `agents/` segment.
4. Disable the new setting and start another session to check that existing naming behavior is preserved.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added await, local-provider command call, Git `for-each-ref` implementation, and folder-isolation early return are directly traced. The only magnitude uncertainty is repository state and Git duration; the eager boundary and first-send reachability are explicit and covered by the added first-send tests.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Extension-host command IPC, Git subprocesses, repository filesystem discovery, and cold repository initialization/status work.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is paid once per new session first send, including folder sessions that never create a branch. The normal warm path performs one `git for-each-ref`; collision retries can perform up to five, while cold/closed repositories add repository-opening work and costs grow with repository/ref size.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased first-prompt latency and avoidable Git CPU/I/O on sessions that do not need a branch.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A folder-isolated session sent its first prompt without invoking the Git extension for branch naming; branch naming work was only relevant if the user later requested PR creation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The first-send path now awaits `_prepareRandomBranchName` whenever the Git settings are enabled and the host advertises the naming property, without checking whether the resolved isolation is `worktree`. The production host advertises that property for both folder and worktree isolation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `const candidate = await this._prepareRandomBranchName(namingResource);` at line 8055 places Git-extension and Git-subprocess work directly before construction and dispatch of the first chat request; the surrounding added condition does not gate on `SessionConfigKey.Isolation`.
Findings.Title: Defer random branch preparation for folder sessions
Findings.Impact: With `chat.agentHost.branchName.useGitSettings` and `git.branchRandomName.enable` enabled, every new folder-isolated local session delays its first prompt on an extension-host round trip and normally one Git subprocess, even when the user never creates a PR. Cold or manually closed repositories can add discovery/opening I/O and compete with an initial status scan, making first-response startup noticeably slower.
Findings.Evidence: `_sendNewSessionRequest` cannot proceed to `sendRequest` until this await completes. For the local provider, `_prepareRandomBranchName` crosses the extension-host command boundary. The new Git command calls `Model.openRepository(..., true, true)` and then `Repository.generateRandomBranchName`, whose collision check invokes `git for-each-ref`; a cold/closed repository can additionally perform repository discovery/opening and schedule a full status. `WorktreeIsolation.resolveWorkingDirectory` returns the original folder without creating a branch when `config[Isolation] !== 'worktree'`, while its schema creates `worktreeBranchNamingProperty` for any Git folder, including folder isolation.
Findings.Recommendation: Gate the awaited preparation to sessions whose effective isolation is `worktree`. For folder sessions, prepare the candidate only when PR creation is requested, or run/persist it off the first-send critical path with ordering that ensures PR creation waits for that preparation.

Scenarios.Scenario: First prompt in a folder-isolated local Agent Host session with Git naming and random names enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `_sendNewSessionRequest` awaits random-name preparation before it constructs and dispatches the chat send request. Folder isolation later returns the original working directory and creates no branch, so this naming work is not required for first-turn progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extension-host command per qualifying first send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Folder-session first send did not invoke the Git extension for branch naming.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fully awaited before the first chat request is sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `git for-each-ref` to collision-check the generated candidate
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normally, up to five sequential attempts on collisions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Git ref lookup for branch naming occurred on folder-session first send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fully awaited through the extension command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover/open the repository and, when cold, initialize it and schedule status
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository resolution per command; warm exact repositories return early, cold repositories perform discovery/open and one queued status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: First send did not force the Git extension to open a closed or undiscovered repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery/opening is awaited; the initial status itself is off the direct await path but competes for Git/I/O resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the first agent chat request
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The request could be dispatched immediately after configuration/eager-create readiness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing request is delayed until all new naming work completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One preparation per new session first send. The normal collision lookup cardinality is one; it can retry up to five times on name collisions. Cold repository cost scales with repository/ref size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The first send is serialized behind the awaited command. Git `Model.openRepository` is sequentialized with repository opens, and collision lookups are sequential retries; there is no coalescing across simultaneous new sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm already-open repository avoids discovery/open initialization but still runs `git for-each-ref`. A cold, closed, or undiscovered repository performs open/discovery and schedules initial status. The generated candidate is persisted per session; failures are not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the await, extension command, Git subprocess, and folder-isolation no-branch path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Git process startup and cold repository-open duration vary by platform and repository; the opt-in population is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression because avoidable Git/IPC work is moved onto first-send latency for sessions that may never create a branch.

Scenarios.Scenario: First prompt and worktree creation in a worktree-isolated local session with random Git naming
Scenarios.CriticalPath: First send awaits candidate generation; host materialization then uses the persisted candidate, checks branch/worktree collisions, and creates the worktree before agent execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate the random candidate via Git extension command
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The host generated a prompt-derived name during worktree creation instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks first-send continuation but supplies the branch needed for imminent worktree creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normally, up to five on collision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No client-side random-name collision check; the host collision check still occurred during creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate a prompt-derived branch hint using utility chat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously up to one per branch creation when a token and prompt were available; zero with a preferred random candidate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Prompt-derived naming could await one utility-model request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff removes this boundary from the random-candidate path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authoritatively check branch existence and create the Git worktree
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one branch check followed by one worktree creation, with bounded collision retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same authoritative host checks and worktree creation ran with prompt-derived names.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One candidate generation and normally one host collision check per new worktree session; retries are bounded by five in each generator. Worktree cost scales with repository size and checkout contents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Candidate generation is awaited and Git repository opening is sequentialized. Host worktree creation is serialized per repository by `_worktreeCreationSequencer`; no aggregate cross-repository limiter is shown, but the diff does not increase worktree creation concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The candidate is generated once and persisted in session config. Warm Git repositories avoid cold opening; there is no shared candidate cache. Host collision checks intentionally revalidate authoritative state at creation time.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both old model-generation and new local-Git paths are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Relative latency depends on local Git speed versus the avoided utility-model request.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: for sessions that immediately need a worktree, the added local lookup supplies required naming and replaces a potentially slower network naming request; authoritative revalidation is necessary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Later pull-request creation from a folder-isolated session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The persisted naming policy is read by the PR handler, which generates/reuses the candidate, checks branch existence, creates/pushes the branch, and performs GitHub PR operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check branch existence and create/push the branch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one collision check plus existing Git branch/push operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: PR creation generated a prompt-derived branch name and performed the same authoritative Git operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One PR API workflow per invocation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One PR operation per user request; candidate collision checks are bounded. The candidate preparation was paid once at first send regardless of whether this scenario occurs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Branch-name collision checks are awaited sequentially. PR Git/network operations follow existing operation ordering; the diff does not add fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first-send candidate is persisted and reused, so it is not regenerated at PR creation. Authoritative branch collision state is checked again because it may have changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: persistence and forwarding are directly added and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The fraction of folder sessions that later create PRs is unknown; sessions that do not are the source of the reported waste.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the eager first-send issue; reuse avoids repeated candidate generation and later authoritative checks are required.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening an existing pull request as an Agent Host worktree session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first-send preparation condition excludes configs with `PullRequestUrl`; the host resolves PR refs and creates the PR worktree through the existing path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same operation; only branch namespace formatting changes when opted in.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One PR checkout per session, with existing GitHub/Git calls independent of random-name settings.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-repository worktree sequencing remains in effect.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Random-name preparation is skipped. Existing repository and PR metadata caches retain their prior behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the explicit `!PullRequestUrl` guard excludes the new preparation boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the diff's performance behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the new eager naming boundary does not run for this scenario.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 23 changed files and all diff pages. Traced first-send, worktree creation, folder-session PR creation, existing-PR checkout, Git extension repository opening, collision retries, persistence, cache state, and sequencing. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity eager-work finding for folder sessions; no qualifying regression fix was identified.
